DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 78 s. 2022 JUL 11 2022 Hon. RUDING GONZALES Vice Mayor, Municipality of Mexico Municipal Hall, Parian Mexico, Pampanga sanggunlangbayanmexico@gmall.com Dear Vice-Mayor Gonzales: This refers to the letter dated 08 March 2022 from then Vice-Mayor Jonathan R. Pangan requesting from the Department a legal opinion on the following queries: I. Should Spouses Titus C. Miclat & Remedios R. Miclat (Spouses Miclat) and Spouses Bryan N. Calma & Ria Anne M. Calma (Spouses Calma), owners of the properties, apply for the reclassification of the five (5) parcels of land or should Silver Palladium Trading Inc., (SPTI) who has the intention to develop the said properties as a digital hub apply for the reclassification of land? And 2. Should the Spouses Calma apply for the reclassification of land that is covered by TCT No. 042-2019022907 which was sold to SPTI as indicated in the notarized Deed of Absolute Sale since the title of the property was not yet transferred to the latter? Per the Letter, Spouses Miclat are the registered owners of four parcels of land in Mexico, Pampanga (Municipality) [Miclat Property]. Spouses Calma, on the other hand, are the registered owners of two parcels of land (Calma Property) within the same jurisdiction. The Miclat and Calma properties are presently classified as agricultural land. SPTI seeks to purchase the parcels of land for the purpose of establishing a digital hub to be known as "Tech City". At the time of the Letter, SPTI has purchased a parcel of land from Spouses Calma pursuant to a Deed of Absolute Sale dated 18 June 2021. The title, however, remains to be under the name of Spouses Calma. The sale of the remaining five parcels of land are still undergoing negotiations between SPTI and their respective owners. Spouses Miclat and Spouses Calma, through their representative, jointly filed an application for the reclassification of the parcels of land registered under their respective names with the Municipality. Hon. Pangan seeks to confirm whether the applicant for reclassification should be the registered owners of the parcels of land, or SPTI as the developer of the same. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), states that it is the Sangguniang Bayan or Sangguniang Panlunsod which may reclassify land within its own jurisdiction. The relevant provisions of the LGC's are as follows: "Section 20. Reclassification of Lands. - (a) (b) (c) (d) (e) A city or municipality may, through an ordinance passed by the sanggunian after conducting public hearings for the purpose, authorize the reclassification of agricultural lands and provide for the manner of their utilization or disposition in the following cases: (1) when the land ceases to be economically feasible and sound for agricultural purposes as determined by the Department of Agriculture or (2) where the land shall have substantially greater economic value for residential, commercial, or industrial purposes, as determined by the sanggunian concerned: Provided, That such reclassification shall be limited to the following percentage of the total agricultural land area at the time of the passage of the ordinance: (1) For highly urbanized and independent component cities, fifteen percent (15%); (2) For component cities and first to the third class municipalities, ten percent (10%); and (3) For fourth to sixth class municipalities, five percent (5%): Provided, further, That agricultural lands distributed to agrarian reform beneficiaries pursuant to Republic Act Numbered Sixty-six hundred fifty-seven (R.A. No. 6657) otherwise known as "The Comprehensive Agrarian Reform LaW', shall not be affected by the said reclassification and the conversion of such lands into other purposes shall be governed by Section 65 of said Act. The President may, when public interest so requires and upon recommendation of the National Economic and Development Authority, authorize a city or municipality to reclassify lands in excess of the limits set in the next preceding paragraph. The local government units shall, in conformity with existing laws, continue to prepare their respective comprehensive land use plans enacted through zoning ordinances which shall be the primary and dominant bases for the future use of land resources: Provided. That the requirements for food production, human settlements, and industrial expansion shall be taken into consideration in the preparation of such plans. Where approval by a national agency is required for reclassification, such approval shall not be unreasonably withheld. Failure to act on a proper and complete application for reclassification within three (3) months from receipt of the same shall be deemed as approval thereof. Nothing in this Section shall be construed as repealing, amending, or modifying in any manner the provisions of R.A. No. 6657." The LGC does not indicate who should be the applicant of applications for reclassification. It is only required that that the same is made by the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) or Sangguniang Panlusod (SP) through an ordinance. Such ordinance shall only be issued upon compliance with the limitations stated in the LGC. Additionally, the steps to reclassify land is further expounded under Office of the President's Memorandum Circular No. 54 (OP-MC No. 54) entitled "Prescribing the Guidelines Governing Sec. 20 of RA 7160 otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 Authorizing Cities and Municipalities to Reclassify Agricultural Lands into Non-Agricultural Uses". Similar to the LGC, however, OP-MC No. 54 merely states that the reclassification of agricultural land must be made through an ordinance by the SP or SB. It does not specify whether the applicant is the owner, purchaser, or developer of the land. Page 2 of 4 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Considering the silence of existing laws, rules and regulations, the SB of the Municipality may, pursuant to its legislative powers, prescribe further guidelines to implement the application for reclassification of agricultural land within its jurisdiction. Verily, its Municipal Ordinance No. 010-2017 entitled "A Municipal Ordinance Enacting the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance of the Municipality of Mexico, Pampanga" reiterates both the LGC and OP-MC No. 54, to wit: "SECTION 41. AGRICULTURAL LAND CONSERVATION AND PRESERVATION CRITERIA - Agricultural lands are recognized as valuable resources that provide employment, amenity and bio-diversity. All agricultural lands in the Municipality shall not be prematurely reclassified. Requests for reclassification shall be evaluated on the merits of conditions prevailing at the time of application, compatibility with the CLUP and subject to the provisions of Memorandum Circular No. 54, Prescribing the Guidelines Governing Section 20 of RA. No. 7160, "Authorizing Cities and Municipalities to Reclassify Agricultural Lands into Non-Agricultural Uses". Applications for agricultural land re-classification approved by the Municipality shall be submitted to the HLURB I Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review and final approval." Pages 308 to 317 of Mexico, Pampanga's 2020 Citizen's Charter, on the other hand, preseribes the checklist of requirements which must be submitted by a person requesting for the reclassification of a parcel of land. We emphasize that among the requirements include: I. Application letter addressed to the Sangguniang Bayan requesting for the reclassification of agricultural land to other purpose; (1 original) 2. Proof of ownership of land such as Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT) / Original Certificate of Title (OCT) and/or other document establishing proof of ownership; ( I photocopy) 3. Special Power of Attorney I Board Resolution/ Secretary's Certificate (If petitioner is other than the owner of the land); (1 original). Based on the Municipality's requirements, it is the owner of the property as stated in the Transfer Certificate of Title which shall file the application for reclassification. We further note that the Citizen's Charter of Mexico Pampanga likewise allows "other document establishing proof of ownership" which may include a Deed of Absolute Sale or other transfer documents. It is therefore the position of this Department that Spouses Miclat and Spouses Calma, or their authorized representative, may apply for the reclassification of the properties titled under their respective names. Meanwhile, either Spouses Calma or SPTI, or their authorized representative, may apply for the reclassification of the one parcel of land which has already been sold to SPTI but still registered under the name of Spouses Calma. Lastly, we take this opportunity to remind the parties of the pronouncements of this Department under its Legal Opinion No. 09, series of 2022 restated below: "Correspondingly, as to the Ordinance reclassifying the land of Barangay Cadulan in the Municipality of Dimasalang, Masbate to residential, commercial, industrial and tourism classifications, -we would like to stress that mere reclassification of an agricultural land does not ipso facto allow the landowner thereof to change its use. Such reclassified agricultural lands must apply for conversion before the Department of Agriculture (DAR) in order to use the same for the said purpose. The Supreme Court, in the case of Chamber of Real Estate and Builders Associations, Inc. (CREBA) V. the Secretary of Agrarian Reform (GR No. 183409) explained: "Reclassification alone will not suffice to use the agricultural lands for other purposes. Conversion is needed to change the current use of reclassified agricultural lands. It is of no moment whether the reclassification of agricultural lands to residential, commercial, industrial or other non-agricultural uses was done by the LGUs or by way of Presidential Proclamations because either way they must still undergo conversion process. It bears stressing that the act of reclassifying agricultural lands to non- agricultural uses simply specifies how agricultural lands shall be utilized for non-agricultural uses and does not automatically convert agricultural lands to non-agricultural uses or for other purposes. As explained in DAR Memorandum Circular No. 7, Series of 1994, cited in the 2009 case of Roxas & Company, Inc. v. DAMBA-NFSW and the Department of Agrarian Reform reclassification of lands denotes their allocation into some specific use and providing for the manner of their utilization and disposition or the act of specifying how agricultural lands shall be utilized for non-agricultural uses such as residential, industrial, or commercial, as embodied in the land use plan. For reclassified agricultural lands, therefore, to be used for the purpose to which they are intended there is still a need to change the current use thereof through the process of conversion. The authority to do so is vested in the DAR, which is mandated to preserve and maintain agricultural lands with increased productivity. Thus, notwithstanding the reclassification of agricultural lands to non-agricultural uses, they must still undergo conversion before they can be used for other purposes." This opinion is rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concerns. Thank you.
